rerun.doctor:
git clone --filter=blob:none https://github.com/Fission-AI/OpenSpec
cd OpenSpec
git checkout 27c0515724decc633818c735ee596481eec78a8b
npx yokoten@0.2.0 doctor --files --json

next.title: Run the checks on every pull request
next.how: a workflow in the folder this project's code host reads (`.github/workflows`, and `.gitea/workflows` too on Gitea) runs `yokoten check` (by its path, or with npx, bunx or pnpm dlx), or has a step that uses yokoten-labs/yokoten
next.why: a commit made with the hook off would reach main unchecked

steps.title: Write the rules for your agents (AGENTS.md)
steps.how: AGENTS.md is at the repo root, and a CLAUDE.md (at the root or in .claude/), when there is one, imports it (`@AGENTS.md`, or `@../AGENTS.md` from .claude/; a Markdown link is not an import): with a CLAUDE.md, Claude Code reads AGENTS.md only through it
steps.why: an agent follows the rules it can read, and only those

steps.title: Turn on the guard for your agents' commands
steps.how: .claude/settings.json has a PreToolUse hook that runs `yokoten hook`. With a .muse/hooks.json, Muse Code must also trust the folder: doctor reads its trust.json, read-only
steps.why: the guard stops a risky command, like a force push, before the agent runs it

steps.title: Add the yokoten runtime to the project
steps.how: .yokoten/VERSION is the version of the yokoten that runs doctor; yokoten's own repo needs no copy
steps.why: the hooks and CI run this copy, so they work with no network and no global install

steps.title: Run your tests on every push
steps.how: package.json has a real "test" script and a `run:` step in a workflow runs it, or a `run:` step starts a test runner such as `node --test`, `go test`, `pytest`, `tox`, `make test` or `npx vitest`; in a workspaces repo, `npm test --workspaces` or `pnpm -r test` counts too
steps.why: tests that run on every push catch a broken change before it reaches main

steps.title: Run the checks on every pull request
steps.how: a workflow in the folder this project's code host reads (`.github/workflows`, and `.gitea/workflows` too on Gitea) runs `yokoten check` (by its path, or with npx, bunx or pnpm dlx), or has a step that uses yokoten-labs/yokoten
steps.why: a commit made with the hook off would reach main unchecked

steps.title: Turn on issues
steps.how: there is no TODO.md, TODO, todo.md or docs/todo
steps.why: an issue has an owner, a state and a history; a todo file has none

steps.title: Add issue and pull request templates
steps.how: .github/ISSUE_TEMPLATE holds a template, and .github holds a pull request template
steps.why: a template asks for what a reviewer needs, so nothing is forgotten

steps.title: Keep build output out of git
steps.how: no tracked file is in a dist/, build/ or out/ folder or is a built file by its name, apart from yokoten.json "allowBuild"
steps.why: a build makes these files again from the source, and a reviewer can't read a binary

steps.title: Keep a changelog
steps.how: CHANGELOG.md has an Unreleased heading, or the repo has a changes/ folder or a .changeset/ folder (Changesets)
steps.why: each pull request adds its entry as it goes, so a release needs no digging

steps.title: Check pull request titles
steps.how: a workflow in the folder this project's code host reads (`.github/workflows`, and `.gitea/workflows` too on Gitea) runs `yokoten check --pr`, or runs on pull requests with a step that uses yokoten-labs/yokoten and does not set `pr-check: false`
steps.why: a pull request title becomes the commit on main, so it must say what changed and why
steps.what: CI does not check pull requests (`yokoten check --pr`)

steps.title: Name the owner (CODEOWNERS)
steps.how: a CODEOWNERS file is in .github/, at the root or in docs/, and the first one GitHub reads names an owner, not init's placeholder @YOUR_GITHUB_HANDLE; full doctor also reads whether the repo belongs to an organization, and an organization alone (@org, not @org/team) is not an owner
steps.why: the host then asks you to review a pull request that changes those paths, and `check --pr` makes it tier A

steps.title: Keep your agents in a sandbox
steps.how: .claude/settings.json turns the sandbox on with no * host; .codex/config.toml pins workspace-write, on-request and no network; .gemini/settings.json blocks YOLO mode; .grok/sandbox.toml holds a workspace profile; writable paths stay in the project
steps.why: a worker writes only where the sandbox allows, so it must cover the worktree

steps.title: Add a license and a security policy
steps.how: a SECURITY.md, a Dependabot config and a license file are in the repo
steps.why: people can then report a hole in private, old dependencies get updates, and others know how they may use the code

files.content:
name: Incident
description: "Something went wrong in how we work. The rca skill turns it into a check. Title: `area: symptom` (what you saw, not the fix), for example `check: misses a key in a JSON file`. At most 60 characters, no full stop, no #N."
title: "area: "
labels: [incident]
body:
  - type: textarea
    id: what
    attributes:
      label: What happened
      description: Facts only, in order, with times in UTC.
    validations:
      required: true
  - type: textarea
    id: matters
    attributes:
      label: Why it matters
      description: "What it cost, or can cost, when it happens again. One or two sentences. `yokoten learn` uses it as the check's reason."
  - type: textarea
    id: why
    attributes:
      label: Why it got through
      description: Which check should have caught it, and why it did not (or that there was none).
  - type: textarea
    id: fix
    attributes:
      label: Fix
      description: What changed so it can't happen again, and the check that now holds it.
  - type: textarea
    id: spread
    attributes:
      label: Other places it can happen
      description: Other projects or paths with the same gap (yokoten).

name: Task
description: "A piece of work. Every change starts here. Title: `area: verb phrase`, for example `doctor: add the review step`. At most 60 characters, no full stop, no #N."
title: "area: "
body:
  - type: textarea
    id: goal
    attributes:
      label: Goal
      description: What is true when this is done, in one or two sentences.
    validations:
      required: true
  - type: textarea
    id: done
    attributes:
      label: Done when
      description: The checks that prove it. A command and its expected output is best.
    validations:
      required: true
  - type: textarea
    id: scope
    attributes:
      label: Out of scope
      description: What this task must not change.
